brief.title: The Yamuna from the Fort to the Taj and Mehtab Bagh

marks.note: The Central Water Commission's warning level
September 2025 at the city's gauge at 2 pm (152.49 m was reported that evening); about the danger level
The record, 1978, and the flood the floodplain notification is reported to refer to

records.what: The highest level on record at the Commission's station.
Reported to lap the Taj's compound walls, for the first time in 45 years.
152.405 m at 2 pm at the city's gauge. Reported 2 to 3 ft of water at Mehtab Bagh and behind the Taj.
A reading well below the warning level, with barrages upstream releasing about 30,000 cusecs.

brief.can_change: land joined to the river at or below the line, except what stays
brief.affects: buildings and streets within a 10-minute walk (800 m on the street network) of the bank
brief.reads: the whole study box, river levels, upstream rain, hot-season surface temperature

links.straight_note: the two gardens face each other across the river
the Mughal riverfront ran between them

open_checks: The floodplain notification of 22 January 2025 and its map. Reported widths of 5.09 km on the right bank and 2.55 km on the left can't be drawn as a line, and read plainly would cover the whole study area. A 2025 report also said the area behind the Taj wasn't demarcated.
Whether a path, a ghat or planting counts as construction under the monument and floodplain rules. Most of this design depends on the answer.
The Archaeological Survey's protected limits, and any monuments here beyond these three.
The Central Water Commission's tables for Agra, the gauge's datum, and a daily record of its level.
The terrain is satellite-derived (FABDEM), good to a couple of metres at best, so any line or height limit drawn from it is rough.
Trees aren't in the view measures, and neither is anything beyond the study area.
Where the riverfront park reported in July 2026 sits.
Whether a rubber dam 1.5 km downstream will be built; it would change the river's low water.

stays.why: A World Heritage monument. Its fabric and its setting are not up for design.
stays.outline: approximate, from the footprints of its main buildings
approximate, from the footprints inside it; its walls are not mapped here

stays.why: The Mughal garden laid out with the Taj, across the river; restored by WMF and ASI.

stays.words: Every building now standing in the zone
stays.why: The design does not remove people's homes or anything else by itself. The floodplain notification is reported to call existing buildings illegal; whether any go is for stakeholders and the courts, not this tool.

stays.words: The view between the Taj and Mehtab Bagh
stays.why: The two gardens were laid out to face each other across the river. What it limits is measured under Read the place.
No channel works are proposed; the design meets the river as it runs.

stays.words: No new building on the floodplain
stays.why: Uttar Pradesh notified the floodplain on 22 January 2025 and is reported to have banned new construction in it, after the National Green Tribunal's orders.
stays.status: reported, the notification itself not read

rules.effect: No construction, except repairs and work under the Act's permissions.
rules.status: the Act read in a copy; drawn from our outlines, not the Archaeological Survey's limits

rules.effect: Construction needs permission, considered by the National Monuments Authority.
rules.status: reported from a High Court ruling; drawn from our outlines

rules.words: 500 m around the Taj, as reported in 2010
rules.effect: One report says no construction within 500 m of the Taj. Not confirmed, so it isn't counted as law here.
New construction banned and existing buildings called illegal, as reported. Its map hasn't been found, so the record flood's reach stands in for it.
rules.status: reported, the notification itself not read

rules.words: Trees within 5 km of the Taj
rules.effect: No felling without the Supreme Court's permission. So planting can be added here, but removing a tree is a matter for the Court.
rules.status: reported May 2025, the order not read

rules.effect: The whole study area lies in it. It limits polluting industry and fuel since 1996; what it asks of a public space hasn't been read.
rules.status: encyclopedia, the Court's orders not read

views.why: The view the garden was made for, along the Taj's axis.
views.status: assumed: an eye at the garden's river edge, and keep the view down to the top of the Taj's plinth, which the terrain reads as about 166 m

views.why: The long view along the river from the Musamman Burj.
views.status: assumed: an eye on the highest terrain at the tower, which satellite terrain may have wrong

views.why: What a visitor sees across the river. Here the limit is the skyline, so that nothing new rises above what is behind it.
views.status: assumed: an eye on the plinth's top as the terrain reads it, looking 40 degrees either side; beyond the study area nothing is counted
